title: A leftover-length Juggler m-cycle can have every local minimum equal to the global minimum
statement: On a Juggler CycleMin of leftover length L (currently 84 or ≥ 85) with m local minima, every valley can equal the global minimum n.
counterexamples: If T^k(n)=n for 0<k<L then follows_take and image_take_of_le give CycleItinerary n (w.take k), a shorter cycle itinerary. Every length < 84 is already excluded, so n occurs once. For m≥2 the other valleys are different odd states and are at least n+2
notes: Unique visit is a reparameterization of prefix return, not a new valley-height law. For m=1 the single valley is n tautologically; height already kills L=84 as a 1-cycle at floor 261. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: leftover L=84 at floor 261; prefix-return argument for every leftover length
